clue.text: Emperor showing rising anger with bishop in legal action

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the whole assembled piece is read upwards, from bottom to top
the anger-and-bishop pair goes inside the word for legal action

parts.note: a suit is a legal action brought in court
ire is anger
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler, furious, sues a churchman in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the whole of SU(IREB)IT upwards, giving TI(BERI)US; it is not just the anger that rises.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the second Roman ruler of that rank, successor to Augustus.

clue.text: Secretary wearing ring with large gem

indicators.note: the ring-and-large pair is worn around the secretary, so it goes outside

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: An office secretary shows off a ring set with a big jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an iridescent precious stone.

clue.text: Dull goody-goody stopping game of cards

indicators.note: stopping here means plugging a gap, so the goody-goody fills the card game

parts.note: stud is a form of poker
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for a goody-goody

explanation.surface: A dreary prig breaks up a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull in the sense of slow-witted or dim.

clue.text: Smart one managed to identify tropical plant

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters are handled and arranged into something new

explanation.surface: A clever person succeeded in naming an exotic plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' looks like a verb of success, but it rearranges SMART ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Swiss cheese plant genus, native to tropical America.

clue.text: Equip old fellow for final battle

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
aged means old
a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: Kit out an elderly academic for the last fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A DON is a university teacher, a fellow of a college at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In Revelation it is the site of the last great conflict between good and evil.

clue.text: Lover I join, right away

indicators.note: away tells us the letter for right is dropped from the joining word

parts.note: to solder is to join metal

explanation.surface: Someone in love says 'I'll unite with you, straight away'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'at once', but 'right' gives R and 'away' removes it from SOLDER.
explanation.definitionFit: She is Tristan's beloved in the medieval romance and Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Report disagreement between inspector and companion

indicators.note: the disagreement sits between the inspector and the companion

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
CH stands for Companion of Honour
a spat is a small quarrel

explanation.surface: A police officer files a note on a row with a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch is an official report, especially one sent from a war zone.

clue.text: Epic poet (not me), great poet

indicators.note: not, with me in brackets, tells us to drop those two letters from the epic poet

parts.note: Homer wrote the Iliad and Odyssey
taken as written, then removed
ace means excellent, great

explanation.surface: A bracketed aside disowns the epic poet in favour of a great one.
explanation.definitionFit: Quintus Horatius Flaccus was a leading Roman lyric writer of odes and satires.

clue.text: King with responsibility about to lead horde's opening charge

indicators.note: the first part comes before what follows
the responsibility goes about the king, surrounding it

parts.note: an onus is a burden or responsibility
R is Rex, king

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of horde

explanation.surface: A king, duty-bound, is about to head the horde's first attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'ready to', but 'about' is the container and 'to lead' joins H on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An onrush is a forward surge or charge.

clue.text: Be dishonest, very, about disguise

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for being dishonest is read backwards

parts.note: to lie is to be dishonest

explanation.surface: Lying very much involves putting on a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil is a covering that masks or hides, as a verb to disguise.

clue.text: Diseased herb, pale, is not going to last long

indicators.note: diseased suggests something unhealthy and out of shape, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A sickly, washed-out plant won't survive for long.
explanation.definitionFit: Perishable goods, like food, decay quickly and cannot be kept.

clue.text: Rascal breaks cover to get clear

indicators.note: the rascal breaks into the cover, splitting it

parts.note: a lid is a cover
an imp is a mischievous rascal

explanation.surface: A naughty child bursts out of hiding to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks cover' is the idiom for leaving a hiding place; here it splits into the container and LID.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid water is transparent and unclouded.

clue.text: One supporting delay in capital punishment ultimately for pirate

indicators.note: the delay and the one go inside the capital

parts.note: Paris is the French capital

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting word sits below, so the one comes after the delay

parts.note: a lag is a delay
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of punishment

explanation.surface: A gibbet-bound buccaneer faces delayed capital punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital punishment' is two pieces: PARIS, and the T at the end of 'punishment'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate in the sense of one who copies others' work and passes it off.

clue.text: Handle latest bit of income, staying in credit, becoming more adept

indicators.note: the handle and the letter stay inside the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
a lever is a handle

indicators.note: the latest bit is the final letter of income

explanation.surface: Managing new income while staying in the black makes one sharper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleverer means smarter, more skilful.

clue.text: Song from soldier perhaps in cast

indicators.note: the soldier goes in the word for cast

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast
a soldier ant is one kind of ant

explanation.surface: A song performed by a soldier, maybe in a theatre cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier perhaps' is a soldier ant, not a man in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea shanty is a sailors' work song.

clue.text: Central point raised in judicial procedure in court

indicators.note: the raised point goes inside the judicial procedure

parts.note: a trial is a judicial procedure

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the central point is turned round

parts.note: the nub is the central point

explanation.surface: The crux of a case comes up during legal proceedings in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body that sits in judgment, a court of justice.

clue.text: Shoe found in wood

definitions.meaning: fragrant timber from an Asian tree

explanation.surface: A shoe turns up in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: One is an open strap-held shoe; the other is the fragrant sandalwood timber, often shortened.

clue.text: Learning about artist in region of France

indicators.note: the learning goes about, surrounding, the artist and the word in

parts.note: lore is traditional learning
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: Study of the painter in a French province.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorraine is a historic north-eastern province of France.

clue.text: Support king received in Lancashire town

indicators.note: the king is taken inside the town's name

parts.note: Bacup is a small town in Lancashire
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is welcomed in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: BACUP is a small mill town in Lancashire, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Backup means support or reinforcement.

clue.text: Party going by car around country

parts.note: a do is a party
the Mini is a small British car
ca, circa, means around

explanation.surface: Revellers drive about a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is not a container here: it gives CA, short for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominica is a Caribbean island nation.

clue.text: Yelp on getting injured in public

indicators.note: being injured bends something out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog yelps as it is hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something openly is doing it without concealment, publicly.

clue.text: Unfounded story, an account rejected by doctor on reflection

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the pair is read backwards
a reflection is a mirror image, so the doctor is read backwards

explanation.surface: A doctor, thinking it over, dismisses a false tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is a groundless rumour or hoax.

clue.text: Minister having vile person put away

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible person
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes in a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant member of the clergy.

clue.text: Material witness first to recognise fool

parts.note: to witness is to see

indicators.note: first to recognise means the first letter of recognise

parts.note: a sucker is a dupe or fool

explanation.surface: A witness is quick to spot a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a puckered cotton fabric.

clue.text: Indicate stone

definitions.meaning: to point out, mark for notice

explanation.surface: Point out the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark something for attention; also a flat paving slab.

clue.text: Loud, bad crowd

parts.note: F is forte, the musical term for loud
ill means bad

explanation.surface: A noisy, unruly mob.
explanation.definitionFit: To crowd a space is to pack or occupy it.

clue.text: State request in a note

indicators.note: the request is placed inside the article and the note

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A formal request is made in a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb, but it is the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the largest US state.

clue.text: Long to get hold of instrument, turning sulky

indicators.note: the word for long gets hold of, contains, the instrument

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it

indicators.note: turning means the instrument's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Someone longs for an instrument and grows moody.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulant means childishly bad-tempered.
